prize_parts.citation: For the conception and leadership of the ATLAS and CMS experiments, which together discovered the Higgs boson at the Large Hadron Collider

statement.case_for: The 2012 observation of a new boson by ATLAS and CMS is a clue from nature in the purest sense: the 2013 prize honoured the theoretical idea, but the experimental discovery that made it a fact has never been recognised. Two independent detectors saw it in several channels, and a decade of coupling measurements has only strengthened the Standard Model reading. Few results in our time are so mature, so unambiguous in content and so central to our picture of the fundamental forces. Having re-read the colleagues' ballots, I still find that no other shortlisted candidate combines this level of certainty about the discovery with this importance for what we know about the universe. The discovery stands first for me; the question is only how to name people behind it.
statement.case_against: The attribution problem is real and I do not wave it away. Thousands of people built and analysed these experiments, and the founding spokespersons and project leaders (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) are a leadership-based reading of credit rather than a clean story of individual insight. If the committee concludes that this is not a prize that individual names can fairly carry, or that the discovery-era spokespersons or accelerator builders were more decisive, then B006 would be better set aside in favour of a candidate whose credit is crisp. Optical lattice clocks (B037) have exactly that crispness, and broader support in the room than my first choice.

responses.point: Ranks optical lattice clocks (B037) first because it is a mature, clearly defined invention with clean two-person attribution (Katori, Ye), already reproduced worldwide and heading towards a redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree that B037 is the cleanest of our candidates on attribution and maturity, and it is my own third choice and my first alternative. Where I differ is on the kind of achievement. The lattice clock is an extraordinary instrument and a probe of constants, but it is a method for measuring, whereas the Higgs result is a discovery about what the world is made of. I also take your point that the Hall and Hänsch and Wineland prizes leave a question about whether this neighbourhood of precision atomic physics is already honoured. I would not block B037, but I do not think the tidiness of its credit should outweigh the importance of what ATLAS and CMS found.

responses.point: Places the Higgs observation (B006) second, as an original experimental discovery completing the Standard Model, but warns that the rules strain against recognising a collaboration and that leadership roles may not be the decisive original contribution.
responses.response: This is the objection I find hardest to answer, and I share it. I think the answer is that for experiments of this scale the conception of the detector, the building of the collaboration and the leadership of the effort are the contribution the prize can recognise, in the way the committee has handled other large-collaboration discoveries. Even so, you are right that the choice of three names is a compromise. I would welcome the committee examining whether Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee remain the right reading, and I would rather say that openly than pretend the credit is clean.

responses.point: Puts magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (B018) first, as a tight link between a quantitative flat-band prediction (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero), reproduced across many groups.
responses.response: The prediction-then-measurement chain is attractive, and I count this as a real discovery of a new platform. My reservation is about maturity: you yourself note that the origin of the superconductivity and of the correlated phases is still debated, and the credit list omits early band-structure work and the lead experimental student. I would want to see how the field looks in some years. That caution does not apply to the Higgs, where the interpretation has been stable for a decade.

responses.point: Ranks gamma-ray burst afterglows (B003) first, valuing an instrument-enabled discovery (BeppoSAX) that settled the cosmological distance scale, with Costa, Frontera and Kulkarni as a coherent triad.
responses.response: I have sympathy for B003 and have placed it as an alternative. It is a clean example of a clue from nature and has an existential dimension, since it connects stellar collapse to the far universe. My qualification is the one you raise yourself: the split between the satellite team and the ground-based follow-up groups is debatable, and at least one important contributor cannot be credited. By that measure B003 is not much better off than B006 on attribution, and it is less central to fundamental physics.

responses.point: Argues for active-matter hydrodynamics (B005) as a simple universal mechanism with long-range order in two dimensions, while conceding that experimental tests of the precise exponents are limited.
responses.response: The intellectual elegance is clear, and I appreciate the Mermin-Wagner point. But my instinct is to want the exponents tested against nature before elevating it, and you concede that this is only partly done; together with the omission of Tu and Simha under the three-name cap, that makes me hesitant to support B005 at this stage.

uncertainties: Whether three leadership names (Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) can fairly stand for two collaborations of thousands, or whether another allocation would be more defensible.
Whether the committee will accept a collaboration-scale discovery as a prize at all, or prefer a candidate with crisper individual credit such as B037.
Whether a two-part prize combining the Higgs discovery with another achievement is feasible, given that the union of names cannot exceed three.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for any shortlisted candidate; my links (David Gross as PhD supervisor, Thomas Van Riet, the Uppsala string group) do not touch these candidates.
